proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the observed-data gradient, strict-borrowing and information-transition results, and uniform mixed-rate constrained-likelihood inference under n rho → infinity, including n rho² → 0; the general results were extended to binary outcomes. Mathematical and decision reviews passed and all three cited leaves were verified, but the cold tier review capped the delivered package at subfield (6.8 versus the field threshold 7.4). No F-stage Lean formalization was attempted; bounded-validation necessity, broader minimax/design results, or estimator implementation and finite-sample/application evidence remain new research.
tldr: The trial ATE has a full observed-data canonical gradient and sharp efficiency bound under conditional control-mean alignment on positive fixed finite alphabets, including binary outcomes. The explicit joint constrained categorical likelihood attains the row bound with uniformly valid studentized inference under \(n\rho_n\to\infty\), allowing arbitrary finite \(U\) and moving source laws. Exact cancellation of the nonempty shape block permits \(n\rho_n^2\to0\); for binary outcomes that block is empty and the same likelihood expansion applies. The survivor criterion, binary-covariate \(\Delta_n^2/\rho_n\) frontier, and distinct zero-validation experiment characterize the precision retained as chart review disappears.
gap: Regular external-control results observe the alignment covariates, and general distribution-alignment results do not by themselves give the mean-only singular experiment. A disappearing validation channel and moving prognostic contrast create a local precision frontier coupled to an unknown external mixture.
fill: The survivor kernel supplies the fixed-law criterion; the focal binary residual lemma derives rank, separation, coordinate invariance, and the correct joint stratum normalization from positive common support. The frontier and a precisely quantified conservative inference theorem isolate the remaining mixed-rate likelihood-expansion question.
